messages:
Jordan Blake: quick q from a couple of us on outbound deals this week — we’re mid pricing experiment on Hosted. can we get a single approved talk track for quoting? prospects keep asking “is this the real price or a test” and “do discounts stack w/ free credits?”

Jordan Blake: specifically: if I give 20% discount on token price + we’re offering promo credits, is it 1) credits then discount on overage? 2) discount applies to everything incl credits? 3) no stacking?

Rachel Kim: +1, CS is getting the same Q on renewals/expansions. we need consistency across AEs/CSMs.

Isabelle Laurent: thanks for flagging. we have 3 open opps w/ experiment variant B right now so we need to stop freelancing answers :grimacing:

Chris Osei: yep. context: experiment is only on Hosted self-serve → sales-assisted is “eligible” if the customer is in the same cohort (same billing org id). we’re trying to avoid hand-created pricing that breaks the measurement.

Jordan Blake: makes sense. but what do I tell them in the moment?

Isabelle Laurent: drafting something now. Nikhil can you confirm how we want to phrase “experiment” vs “promo” and what is locked in on an order form?

Nikhil Sharma: for talk track, please avoid saying “we’re testing prices on you” lol. position as: “We’re running a limited-time promotional packaging offer for new Hosted customers in certain segments; we’ll quote you in writing and honor it for the quote term.”

Nikhil Sharma: we can honor pricing on an order form; self-serve without an order form is always “per our pricing page”, subject to change.

Jordan Blake: ok but the stacking rule?

Laura Bennett: Finance view (and what we can defend cleanly): promo credits are a one-time credit balance. they reduce billable usage first. discounts apply to the remaining billed amount (post-credit). we should not “discount” the credits themselves.

Isabelle Laurent: +1. simplest: credits are applied before discounts; discount applies to overage/paid usage only. (Operationally: invoice shows usage at rate, then credit line, then discount line on net charges.)

Chris Osei: small correction: current billing implementation applies credits to *charges* (not raw tokens) at invoice time. outcome is the same: credits reduce the amount due first, then any contractual discount is calculated on net remaining charges.

Jordan Blake: got it. so: credits first, then discount on remainder. any exceptions?

Sofia Mendes: legal note: don’t promise “credits + discount stack” as a blanket statement unless it’s explicitly in the order form. if you include a promotional credit, it should be a separate line item with a defined term + “no cash value / non-transferable” language. also we should avoid “most favored customer” implications by implying this is the default for everyone.

Isabelle Laurent: ok, here’s proposed “approved talk track” (please poke holes):
- “Your usage is billed based on metered tokens/requests per our standard definitions. For this quote, we’re including (a) a promotional credit balance and/or (b) a discounted usage rate.”
- “Promotional credits apply to reduce billed charges first. Any negotiated % discount applies to remaining charges after credits are consumed.”
- “Credits do not change how usage is metered; they’re a billing adjustment on the invoice.”
- “We’ll document everything in the order form and honor it for the quote validity period (typically 30 days).”

Rachel Kim: can we add a line about what happens after the promo period? customers always ask.

Nikhil Sharma: add: “After the promotional period, your account continues on standard pricing unless we renew or amend the offer in writing.”

Jordan Blake: and for the “experiment” wording: say “promo packaging offer”, not “experiment”.

Chris Osei: yes. internally it’s an experiment; externally it’s an offer. BUT make sure AE notes include the experiment flag so RevOps can attribute results.

Isabelle Laurent: +1. operational instructions for AEs:
1) in Salesforce, populate: `Pricing experiment` = H1-2026-Hosted-CreditsOverage (picklist)
2) attach latest quote template v7 (has promo credit clause + measurement language)
3) if customer asks for “discount on top of credits” beyond standard, escalate to Sales Ops + Finance for approval.

Dev Patel: support angle: please avoid saying “console may differ from invoice”. say: “Console and invoice should match; if anything looks off we can reconcile using request IDs and usage export.” we’ve had a couple tickets where the phrasing triggered distrust.

Jordan Blake: good call.

Laura Bennett: one more guardrail: if you’re offering both credits + discount, keep the combined effective value within your normal approval band. don’t use credits as a workaround to bypass discount approval.

Isabelle Laurent: :thumbsup: I’ll post this as the interim guidance in #sales pins once Nikhil signs off.

Nikhil Sharma: signed off. also please don’t negotiate “retroactive credits if you don’t like the results” — that breaks measurement.

Sofia Mendes: adding: dispute window language is in the template; don’t edit it ad hoc. if customer redlines measurement/audit rights, route to Legal.

Jordan Blake: awesome. can you drop the link to the template + the talk track?

Isabelle Laurent: links:
- Quote template v7 (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-sales-quote-templates (v7)
- Internal FAQ draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SALES/Pricing+%2B+Metering+FAQ (WIP)
- Enablement deck draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/pricing-change-enablement-deck (slides)

Rachel Kim: can we get a short version for CSMs too? like 3 bullets.

Isabelle Laurent: short version:
1) We’re offering promo credits and/or discounted usage rates, documented in the order form.
2) Credits reduce billed charges first; discounts apply to remaining charges.
3) Metering is unchanged; if anything looks off, we can reconcile via usage export/request IDs.

Chris Osei: I’ll also update the experiment registry to reflect “external positioning = promo offer” so we’re aligned.

Jordan Blake: thanks all. I’ll use this on my 2pm call.

Isabelle Laurent: pls reply in-thread if you get weird objections so we can keep tightening the language.

Salesforce Bot: (auto) Jordan Blake updated Opportunity “Northwind AI - Hosted Pilot” field `Pricing experiment` → H1-2026-Hosted-CreditsOverage

Jordan Blake: lol perfect timing :joy: :thumbsup:
